headline.en: You already carry these leaps in songs you know.

detail.en: Do to mi: a leap of three
So below to do: a leap of four
Do to so: a leap of five

text.en: Echo each leap: Saints, Amazing Grace, then Twinkle. Each starts with its key's chord.
Round 1: the guide sings the first note. You sing it, then the leap.
Round 2: the same three leaps, from new notes. Same tune, new note.

measures.en: Your stars are for finding each leap from a new note: the note you sang has to be the leap that was asked, close to its middle.

title.en: Up or down, step or leap

headline.en: Two questions about every new note: up or down, and near or far?

detail.en: Higher or lower than the last
The next note along: do to re
Skipping notes: do to mi, or further

text.en: Each clip starts with the key's chord. Listen as often as you like, then choose.

prompt.en: Does it go up or down?

why.en: Do to mi: up a leap of three.

prompt.en: Does it go up or down?

why.en: So to mi: down.
A is do to mi, three. B is do to so, five: bigger.
A is a leap of four. B is a step.
Do to re: the next note along, a step.
Mi to so skips fa: a leap.

text.en: The scale with numbers: do (1) up to so (5) and back. Echo it.
Now shapes: echo each one, up and down.

measures.en: Your stars are for every note of the shapes landing close to its middle.

headline.en: A leap of three is Saints. A leap of five is Twinkle. Hear the tune, know the leap.

detail.en: Oh when the saints
Twinkle, twinkle
Amazing Grace, in between

text.en: Each clip starts with the key's chord. Which leap is it?

why.en: Do to mi: three, like Oh When the Saints.
Do to so: five, like Twinkle.
So below to do: four, like Amazing Grace.
Three again, in a new key: still Saints.
Five, in a new key: still Twinkle.
Four: so to do in this key, like Amazing Grace.

text.en: From new notes: the guide gives the first, you sing it and the leap the screen names.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing the leap each time, the note you sang being the one asked, close to its middle.

text.en: Your six leaps from Song starts, to see how far you've come.
Which leap is it?

why.en: Re to so here is so to do in its own key: four.
Three: do to mi in its key.
Five: do to so.
Four: Amazing Grace.
Five, from a new note.
Three: the Saints.

text.en: The guide gives a note; sing the leap the screen names.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing each leap the screen named, the note you sang being the one asked, close to its middle.

headline.en: A leap of four is Amazing Grace. A leap of five is Twinkle: one step wider, and it vibrates three to two.

detail.en: A-ma-zing
Twinkle, twinkle
Four sounds like coming home

text.en: Each clip starts with the key's chord. Four or five?

why.en: So below to do: four, like Amazing Grace.
Do to so: five, like Twinkle.
Four, in a new key: so to do.
Five, in a new key: do to so.
Three, from before: the Saints.
Five: do to so in this key.

text.en: The guide gives a note; sing the leap the screen names.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing each leap asked, the note you sang being the one asked, close to its middle.

headline.en: A whole step is two piano keys apart; a half step is the very next key. Ode to Joy has both.

detail.en: Mi, mi, fa, so: a half step, then a whole step
Do to re: a whole step
Mi to fa, and ti to do

text.en: Each clip starts with the key's chord. Half step or whole step?

why.en: Mi to fa: a half step, the closest two notes in the scale.
Do to re: a whole step, Frère Jacques.
Fa to so: a whole step, the end of Ode to Joy's start.
Ti below to do: a half step, leaning home.
Re down to do: a whole step.
From before: do to mi, a leap of three.

text.en: Sing the step the screen names, from the guide's note.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing each leap asked, the note you sang being the one asked, close to its middle.

headline.en: A leap of three comes big or small. The Saints' is big and bright; Greensleeves' is small and dark.

detail.en: Do to mi: Oh when the saints
La below to do: Greensleeves
That half step is the difference

text.en: Each clip starts with the key's chord. Big three or small three?

why.en: Do to mi: big, like the Saints.
La below to do: small, like Greensleeves.
Re to fa: small.
Big: do to mi in its own key.
Mi to so: small.
From before: four, Amazing Grace.

text.en: Sing the three the screen names, from the guide's note.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing each leap asked, the note you sang being the one asked, close to its middle.

headline.en: A leap of six is My Bonnie. Eight is the octave: the same note, higher, vibrating exactly twice as fast.

detail.en: My Bon-nie
The same note, higher
So the top stays easy

text.en: Each clip starts with the key's chord. Five, six or an octave?

why.en: So below to mi: six, My Bonnie.
So below to so: the same note, higher.
Do to so: five, Twinkle.
Six, in a new key.
Five, from a low note.
The octave: it sounds like the same note.

text.en: Sing the leap the screen names. Big leaps start low.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing each leap asked, the note you sang being the one asked, close to its middle.

headline.en: The same leaps, falling. Each has its song too.

detail.en: Mi to do: Swing Low
So to mi: This Old Man
O Come, All Ye Faithful; Twinkle backwards

text.en: Each clip starts with the key's chord. Which leap, going down?

why.en: Mi to do: three down, Swing Low.
Do to so below: four down, O Come, All Ye Faithful.
So to do: five down, Twinkle backwards.
So to mi: a small three down, This Old Man.
Four down, in a new key.
Up: so below to do, Amazing Grace.

text.en: Sing the leap down the screen names, from the guide's note.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing each leap asked, the note you sang being the one asked, close to its middle.

headline.en: A chord's middle note, its third, decides whether it sounds bright (major) or dark (minor).

detail.en: A big three, then a small one
A small three, then a big one; "me" is said "may"
By a half step

text.en: Listen as often as you like: major or minor?

why.en: Bright: major.
Darker: minor.
Do, mi, so: major.
Do, me, so: minor.
Minor, on another note.
Major, from a lower note.
Minor: the middle note is a small three up.
B: its middle note is a half step lower.

text.en: Echo each broken chord: major, then minor, and hear the middle note move.

measures.en: Your stars are for every note of the chords landing close to its middle, most of all the third that makes it major or minor.

headline.en: The guide sings so and do. You sing the middle note: mi for major, me for minor.

detail.en: A big three above do: bright
A small three above do: dark
Listen as you sing it

text.en: The guide sings so and do; sing the third the screen names. Did you hear it change colour?

measures.en: Your stars are for singing the third asked, mi or me, the note you sang being that one, close to its middle.

headline.en: Change one note and a happy tune turns sad. Hear Frère Jacques and Twinkle both ways.

detail.en: Do, re, mi, do, or do, re, me, do
The la turns to le
Only the third moved

text.en: Which one is minor?

why.en: B sings me, not mi: minor.
A's high notes are a half step lower: minor.
Minor: me in the third note.
Major: the usual Twinkle.
A: Frère Jacques in minor, from a new note.
From before: five, Twinkle.

text.en: Frère Jacques' first line in minor: echo it twice.

measures.en: Your stars are for every note landing close to its middle, the me most of all.

headline.en: The guide sings a chord's root and fifth; you fill in the third, through home, four, five and home.

detail.en: Do and so; you sing mi
Do and fa; you sing la, below
So below and re; you sing ti, below

text.en: Your six leaps from Song starts, to see how far you've come.
Try it: the guide sings the root and fifth, then the third. Echo all three.
Now fill the middle on your own: the guide sings root and fifth, you sing the third.

measures.en: Your stars are for singing each chord's third, the note you sang being that one, close to its middle.
